blocks.raw: #### What is Data Import Framework?
blocks.text: What is Data Import Framework?

blocks.raw: The Data Import Framework is a web application that helps you upload offline data generated at stores to the Capillary Database.
blocks.text: The Data Import Framework is a web application that helps you upload offline data generated at stores to the Capillary Database.

blocks.raw: When InStore is operated online, it continuously syncs data generated at the PoS to the Capillary Database. However, if data is not captured through InStore but saved in the PoS machines, you can use the Data Import Framework to upload such data to the Capillary Database.
blocks.text: When InStore is operated online, it continuously syncs data generated at the PoS to the Capillary Database. However, if data is not captured through InStore but saved in the PoS machines, you can use the Data Import Framework to upload such data to the Capillary Database.

blocks.raw: **Note:** Customers imported using the Data Import Framework will appear in the new Member Care (Cortex) search only after the daily Cortex sync, which occurs at 12 AM cluster timezone. Customers registered through APIs are available in Cortex search immediately due to event-driven sync. This timing difference is due to Cortex data ingestion processes.

blocks.raw: #### How can I import data to the Capillary Database?
blocks.text: How can I import data to the Capillary Database?

blocks.raw: Based on the size of the data, you can import data in two ways:
blocks.text: Based on the size of the data, you can import data in two ways:

blocks.raw:
* Import directly: If the number of entries in the CSV file are less than 700,000, you can directly upload the data (.csv) file in Data Import Framework.
* Import through an FTP server: If the number of entries in the csv file are from 700,000 to 1,000,000, you need to import data from an FTP server. For this, you need to provide read/write access to a specific directory of the FTP Server and schedule the import job on a daily, weekly or monthly basis.

blocks.raw:
> \[!NOTE]
> **Positional mapping in CSV imports**
>
> The import framework uses positional mapping, not header-based mapping, when processing CSV files. This means column values are read strictly based on their order in the file, regardless of the column names.
>
> If the column order in the CSV does not match the expected schema, values may be validated against the wrong fields and the record can fail silently or be rejected.
>
> **Example:**
> If comm\_channel and sub\_status columns are swapped, values like EMAIL and OPTOUT will be validated against incorrect enums, resulting in import failures.
>
> Always ensure the CSV column order exactly matches the expected template sequence before uploading files.

blocks.raw:
> 🚧 **Large imports running during peak hours can cause live API timeouts**
>
> The Data Import Framework writes directly to the Capillary database tables that also serve live API traffic, including `v1.1/points/redeem` and `v2/customers`. When a large import runs during peak hours, it creates contention on these shared tables. API calls that write to the same tables may time out and return 520 errors for end users. Loyalty customer profile imports carry the highest risk because they touch the loyalty table directly.
>
> Schedule all imports exceeding 200,000 records during the off-peak window (10 PM to 6 AM cluster timezone). Do not trigger large imports during business hours even if the system allows it.

blocks.raw:
* **Data Transformer & Transformer Inputs**\
  This option is used to modify the existing data in a column automatically by making use of the functions and other configurations.
blocks.text: Data Transformer & Transformer InputsThis option is used to modify the existing data in a column automatically by making use of the functions and other configurations.

blocks.raw: There are four types of data transformers as mentioned in the following table.
blocks.text: There are four types of data transformers as mentioned in the following table.

blocks.raw:
Data Transformers Description
Merge Merges the values of two or more columns to a single field. Write the merge function in the **Transformer Inputs** box. Columns=>x,y,z or Columns=>2,3,4;Separator=>[] where x, y and z are column numbers. For example, if Column=>1,2,3 is set then the text in the columns 1, 2, 3 will be merged to a single field separating each column with a comma (,), a default value. You can set any delimiter for merging two or more columns using the Separator=> function. For example, if Column=>1,2,3;Separator=>; is set in **Transformer Inputs**, the columns 1, 2 and 3 will be merged separating the value of each column with a semicolon.
Default Value Replaces null values present in the column with a value specified in Transformer Inputs. Value=>[Any Value]. For example, if Value=>store.server is set in **Transformer Inputs**, all null values identified in the column will be replaced with 'store.server'
Convert to Date & Time Changes the date and time format across the column. This is applicable only to the columns with date and time. Set the standard date and time format in the **Transformer Inputs**box. **Date parameters** * d - Day of the month (1-31) * m - Month (1-12) * Y - Year in four digits (example: 2013) * y: Year (13) **Time Parameters** * H: Hours (24hr format) * s: Seconds * h: 12 hour format(1-12) * i: Minutes (00 - 60) The parameters of date and time format can be used in any order. For example, date can be set as d/m/Y or m/d/Y or Y/m/d. However, it is recommended to use the standard date and time format of the organization.
Expression This function lets you apply some mathematical calculations on two or more columns. Exp=>\{Column no. of A} \{+ or - or *or /} \{Column no. of B} For example, if the expression is set to Exp=>\{1}\{2}-10, All null values of that column will be replaced with - (value of that field will be (value of column 1) * (value of column2) - 10). You can use this function only on columns with integer values but not for string data types.

When a large import runs during peak hours, it creates contention on these shared tables. API calls that write to the same tables may time out and return 520 errors for end users. Loyalty customer profile imports carry the highest risk because they touch the loyalty table directly.
>
> Schedule all imports exceeding 200,000 records during the off-peak window (10 PM to 6 AM cluster timezone). Do not trigger large imports during business hours even if the system allows it.

blocks.raw:

* Create and configure templates for each profile that you want to import
* Create different folders for each profile type in the FTP server
* Copy data files of each profile to the respective folder of the FTP server. For example, registration data in Registration folder, points redemption data in the Points Redeem folder and so on
* Map the fields in the database to the respective column names of the CSV file
* Perform a trial import for each profile type
* Perform the actual import job

blocks.raw: ## Limitations
blocks.text: Limitations

blocks.raw: \###Cluster-level idle-time SLA for FTP imports
blocks.text: ###Cluster-level idle-time SLA for FTP imports

blocks.raw:
* The platform enforces a cluster-level idle-time SLA for queued FTP imports. If an import remains in the queue beyond this SLA, the platform marks it as Fail by validator (FTP TEMPDB\_FAILED), even if the file contains no validation errors.
* The platform processes FTP imports one at a time for each organization and profile. Submitting many large files in a single batch can delay processing and cause later imports to exceed the idle-time SLA.
* The platform does not retry imports that fail because they exceed the idle-time SLA. Re-upload and reschedule these files to process them again.
* To reduce the risk of idle-time SLA failures, submit smaller batches of files and avoid uploading many large files at the same time.

blocks.raw: \###Per-file record limit for direct upload
blocks.text: ###Per-file record limit for direct upload

blocks.raw: * The number of records allowed per file for direct upload is subject to a cluster-level configuration that may vary by org. The default limit is 15,000 records per file for some profiles. If your file exceeds this limit, the import is rejected with a validation error before processing begins. To increase the per-file limit for your org, raise a request with the Capillary sustenance team. Note that this limit is separate from the overall 24-hour direct import cap of 200,000 records.

To increase the per-file limit for your org, raise a request with the Capillary sustenance team. Note that this limit is separate from the overall 24-hour direct import cap of 200,000 records.

blocks.raw: \###Only one import job per profile can run at a time
blocks.text: ###Only one import job per profile can run at a time

blocks.raw:
* The Data Import Framework allows only one active import job per profile per org at any given time. If you attempt to start a new import while a previous job for the same profile is still in progress (including the temporary database stage), the system rejects the new attempt with an error indicating that an import is already running. Wait for the current job to reach a terminal state (completed or failed) before submitting the next batch. If a job appears stuck, do not attempt to start a new import until you have confirmed the status of the existing job on the Import File Details page.
  \###Understanding the TEMP\_DB\_COMPLETED status
  TEMP\_DB\_COMPLETED means the file has been loaded into the temporary database but has not yet been pushed to the main database. At this stage, no records have been permanently written and the data is not yet visible in Member Care. It is safe to proceed with "Import to Main DB" — re-triggering this step does not re-process records that were already successfully written to the main database in a prior attempt. If you are unsure whether a previous "Import to Main DB" run completed, check the Import File Details page for the job status before proceeding.

blocks.raw: ## Handling encrypted data during data ingestion
blocks.text: Handling encrypted data during data ingestion

blocks.raw: The configuration CONF\_IS\_PII\_ENCRYPTED controls whether the system expects PII identifiers to be provided in encrypted form during data ingestion.
blocks.text: The configuration CONF_IS_PII_ENCRYPTED controls whether the system expects PII identifiers to be provided in encrypted form during data ingestion.

blocks.raw: When enabled, the system treats PII fields as opaque encrypted strings. It bypasses all validation and formatting logic for these fields to avoid rejecting or modifying encrypted values.
blocks.text: When enabled, the system treats PII fields as opaque encrypted strings. It bypasses all validation and formatting logic for these fields to avoid rejecting or modifying encrypted values.

blocks.raw: This configuration is intended for integrations where PII is encrypted at the source before being sent to the platform.
blocks.text: This configuration is intended for integrations where PII is encrypted at the source before being sent to the platform.

blocks.raw: ## Behaviour
blocks.text: Behaviour

blocks.raw:
* Skips validation checks (length, pattern, format)

* Skips data cleaning and normalisation

* Stores values exactly as received (with safe transformations only)

* Prevents corruption of encrypted identifiers
